Hello, Flavia. This is Lorenzo Conti, from the trade association in Verona. Thank you for the documents. Before our meeting on Monday, I want to share three concerns from our members. First, the price. Brazilian products are far away, so the transport is expensive. Second, quality. Our buyers want proof that every product meets European standards. Third, the timeline. They want to see results in less than one year. I am not saying no. I am saying that we need clear answers. See you on Monday.

Objections are not a bad sign. When a partner pushes back, it often means that they are interested. Here is a simple method. First, acknowledge the concern. Say: I understand your concern. Do not argue right away. Second, clarify. Ask a question to understand the real problem. Third, reframe. Show the idea from a different point of view. Finally, if you believe in your position, keep it, politely. And if you need time, it is fine to pause. A short silence is better than a weak answer.

First, I listen to the objection and I do not interrupt. Then, I acknowledge the concern: I understand your concern. Next, I ask a question to clarify the real problem. After that, I reframe the idea: let me put it a different way. Finally, I keep my position politely and I propose a next step.
